label: Lemmy
terms_note: Bots must self-flag (bot_account) and need the community's permission; promotional posting is banned on most instances; federated content cannot be recalled from other instances.

auth: 1. Account on the user's chosen instance (registration may need an application / captcha); set

endpoints.call: POST /post` {name, community_id, body (markdown), url, nsfw, language_id, alt_text}

reference.limits: - Rate limits are instance settings (`rate_limit_message`, `_post`, `_comment`, `_search`, `_image`, `_register` with per-second windows) — read them from `GET /site` (`local_site_rate_limit`). - Each instance and community publishes rules; promotional posts are widely banned and bots need explicit permission; content federates (ActivityPub) and cannot be recalled from other instances.

fields.name: username_or_email
fields.help: Username or e-mail of the account on its instance; sent as `username_or_email` to POST https://<instance>/api/v3/user/login (Login {username_or_email, password, totp_2fa_token?}, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LemmyNet/lemmy-js-client/0.19.4/src/types/Login.ts).

fields.name: password
fields.help: The account's password. The runtime exchanges it for the LoginResponse `jwt` (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LemmyNet/lemmy-js-client/0.19.4/src/types/LoginResponse.ts) and sends 'Authorization: Bearer <jwt>' (lemmy-js-client setHeaders pattern); the token is cached for a day and re-issued on expiry or 401. Accounts with TOTP enabled cannot log in this way (totp_2fa_token is not sent). Mark automated accounts as bot_account in the profile settings.

config_fields.name: instance
config_fields.help: Host of the account's Lemmy instance without scheme, e.g. lemmy.ml; every call (including the login) goes to https://<instance>/api/v3/... (the v3 API served by the 0.19.x release line that public instances run; Lemmy 1.0's /api/v4 is not covered).

config_fields.name: community_id
config_fields.help: Numeric id of the community the account posts to (CreatePost.community_id, an integer: shown by GET https://<instance>/api/v3/community?name=<name> as community_view.community.id); sent as a JSON integer on publish_text / publish_image. Env PLATFORM_MCP_LEMMY_COMMUNITY_ID.

adapter.rate_note: Rate limits are per instance and configured by its admins (message, post, register, image, comment, search and import buckets in the site's local_site_rate_limit, returned under site_view.local_site_rate_limit by GET /api/v3/site); 429 answers are honoured via Retry-After. One client-side bucket at 2/s.

me.note: GET /api/v3/site with the session token returns GetSiteResponse {site_view, admins, version, my_user, all_languages, ...}; the connected account is account.my_user (MyUserInfo: local_user_view.person {id, name, display_name, actor_id, bot_account, ...}, follows, moderates). Wrong credentials fail at the login step (auth_error); the login itself is the credential check, because /site also answers anonymously and silently ignores an invalid token (checked live on lemmy.ml 0.19.20).

read_comments.note: GET /api/v3/comment/list?post_id=&page=&limit= (GetComments: type_, sort, max_depth, page, limit, community_id, community_name, post_id, parent_id, saved_only, liked_only, disliked_only) returns GetCommentsResponse {comments: CommentView[]} where each CommentView carries comment {id, creator_id, post_id, content (markdown), published, updated, deleted, removed, ap_id, path, ...}, creator (Person {id, name, display_name, actor_id, ...}), post, community and counts (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LemmyNet/lemmy-js-client/0.19.4/src/types/CommentView.ts). `sort` and `max_depth` are not sent (instance defaults: a flat page of the post's comments). Lemmy's server-side page size is 1..50 (FETCH_LIMIT_MAX = 50, 'Fetch limit is > 50' otherwise; default 10, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LemmyNet/lemmy/0.19.4/crates/db_schema/src/utils.rs), so `limit` is capped at 50; `page` is 1-based.

read_mentions.note: GET /api/v3/user/mention?page=&limit= (GetPersonMentions: sort, page, limit, unread_only; needs the token) returns GetPersonMentionsResponse {mentions: PersonMentionView[]} with person_mention {id, recipient_id, comment_id, read, published}, comment, creator, post, community, recipient, counts (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LemmyNet/lemmy-js-client/0.19.4/src/types/PersonMentionView.ts). `id` is the mentioning comment's id (the mention record's own id is raw.person_mention.id); `since` is not a documented parameter and is not sent; `unread_only` is not sent, so read mentions are included. Same 1..50 page size as read_comments.

analytics_post.note: GET /api/v3/post?id=<post id> (GetPost: id or comment_id) returns GetPostResponse {post_view, community_view, moderators, cross_posts}; the counts come from post_view.counts (PostAggregates {post_id, comments, score, upvotes, downvotes, published, newest_comment_time}). The runtime cannot compose a nested `metrics` object, so counts are top-level fields; the post itself is not under raw (raw is the counts object).

publish_text.note: POST /api/v3/post (CreatePost {name, community_id, url?, body?, alt_text?, nsfw?, language_id?, ...}) returns PostResponse {post_view{post{id, name, body, ap_id, published, ...}, creator, community, counts}}. Lemmy posts need a title, so `text` is sent as `name` AND as the markdown `body`; the title must be 3-200 characters without a newline (is_valid_post_title, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LemmyNet/lemmy/0.19.4/crates/utils/src/utils/validation.rs) or the instance answers 400 invalid_post_title (upstream_error), and the body may be up to 50,000 characters. The post goes to the configured community_id (sent as a JSON integer). `reply_to` is ignored: posts cannot reply (use reply_comment-style comments via POST /comment, not offered). `id` is the post id used by read_comments / analytics_post / delete; `url` is the post's ActivityPub id (its canonical URL on the home instance).

publish_image.note: A Lemmy image post is a link post: CreatePost {name, community_id, url} with `url` = the first image URL (image_urls[0]; Lemmy fetches the link's metadata and thumbnail server-side, and instances render image URLs inline). Only ONE url fits a post, so further image_urls are ignored. `text` is REQUIRED here in practice because it becomes the mandatory `name` (title, 3-200 characters, no newline); without it the instance answers 400. Same response mapping as publish_text.

delete.note: POST /api/v3/post/delete (DeletePost {post_id: PostId, deleted: boolean}) marks the account's own post deleted and returns PostResponse {post_view} (under raw; the runtime answers {status: 'deleted'}). `post_id` is sent as a JSON integer (a non-numeric id is an invalid_input); deleting someone else's post is refused by the instance with a 400 (upstream_error). Deletion federates best-effort: 'federated content cannot be recalled from other instances'.

not_offered.reply_comment: POST /api/v3/comment needs CreateComment {content, post_id: PostId (required), parent_id?: CommentId} (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LemmyNet/lemmy-js-client/0.19.4/src/types/CreateComment.ts): a reply must name the POST it belongs to, the vocabulary passes only the comment's id, and the runtime cannot look the post up first (GET /api/v3/comment?id= would be a second call), so the request cannot be composed.

evidence: host lemmy.ml: DNS ok, TLSv1.3 (Let's Encrypt)
probe: 7/7 tools answered on their documented path with an auth refusal, a validation error or data; control route -> 404 (not_found), so the answers are path-specific
HTML docs spot-check (render-doc): 0/6 tool paths found verbatim on their docs pages; names not found on the page: analytics_post:id
live read without credentials: analytics_post, read_comments returned data that validates against the vocabulary
